clue.text: Introduces air with a couple of notes on speeds

parts.note: A and E are two notes of the musical scale
rates are speeds, as in rates of knots

explanation.surface: Someone adds a comment about tempo, perhaps a musician marking up a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate something is to pump or mix oxygen-bearing gas into it.

clue.text: Retired painter takes it easy, then stops

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the word for painter is read backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter
to take it easy is to rest, so rests

explanation.surface: An old artist relaxes in retirement and then gives up work altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns RA (Royal Academician, a crossword painter) into AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arresting something halts it, so arrests is a synonym of stops (verb).

clue.text: Excursion or a tour visits New Zealand lake city

indicators.note: an excursion is a wandering trip, so the letters of the following words wander out of order

explanation.surface: A sightseeing trip takes in a city by a lake in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excursion' rearranges ORATOUR, the letters of 'or a tour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotorua is a North Island city standing on the lake of the same name, known for geysers.

clue.text: Lean on good leader who has a slight obsession

parts.note: lean as an adjective means thin

indicators.note: a word's leader is its opening letter, here the first of good

explanation.surface: A coach leans on a capable captain who is a little fixated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean on' looks like a verb phrase of pressure; 'Lean' is the adjective THIN, and 'on' just sets G after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is an idiom for a mild fixation.

clue.text: Fish after entree was quite a surprise!

indicators.note: after places the fish word behind the entree word

parts.note: an entree is an entrance or a start
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: The fish served after the starter course turned out to be a real shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entree' suggests a starter course at dinner; here it means an entry, a START.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was startling was a real shock; the adjective fills the place of the phrase after 'was'.

clue.text: Girl 'e drools about

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A Cockney complains that some man is slobbering everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges EDROOLS, the letters of ''e drools', the apostrophe adding nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolores is a female first name, of Spanish origin.

clue.text: Bloom is found in 24 hrs

indicators.note: found in tells us the little word is placed inside the other

parts.note: twenty-four hours make a day

explanation.surface: A flower is said to open and close within a day.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' looks like a reference to clue 24; it is just twenty-four hours, a DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy is a common flower, and bloom means a flower.

clue.text: Fish found on fruit only

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: A fish dish comes with nothing but a citrus garnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a European flatfish eaten widely.

clue.text: Auden or, possibly, a poem he wrote

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The poet W H Auden might have composed a certain verse form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AUDENOR, the letters of 'Auden or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form with a refrain, the kind of piece a poet might compose.

clue.text: Lister made exciting start, but it was unfruitful

indicators.note: made signals the name is reworked into a new word
start names the opening letter of exciting

explanation.surface: Joseph Lister began his work with a thrill, yet nothing came of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges LISTER into STERIL; 'start' of 'exciting' gives E. Lister, the antiseptic pioneer, makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile land or creatures produce no offspring or crop, barren.

clue.text: Mixed nastier drink

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mixed cocktail turns out even more unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges the letters of 'nastier'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: I am accompanying chaps to London area, it's vast!

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
chaps are men
SE is a London postal district, south-east

explanation.surface: Someone joins some men heading to a part of London and marvels at its size.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is the south-east London postcode area.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means enormous, so huge in extent.

clue.text: Look about, right and left, in a jaunty manner

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the look word goes around the others

parts.note: to spy is to look

explanation.surface: Someone glances around in every direction with a spring in the step.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and brisk, the manner of a jaunty walk.

clue.text: Anna evidently has some birthmarks

indicators.note: has some says the phrase contains a run of letters to be taken out

explanation.surface: A woman called Anna clearly has a few marks on her skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of naevus, the medical word for a birthmark, is Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi are coloured skin marks present from birth, moles.

clue.text: The wine got left inside which was very remiss

indicators.note: inside places the letter for left within the wine word

parts.note: sack is an old name for fortified white wine like sherry

explanation.surface: Someone left the wine to spoil, a careless act.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is the old word for sherry-type wine, as drunk by Falstaff.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack means negligent or lax, careless in duty.

clue.text: Bird caused cat, we hear, to sit up and take notice

indicators.note: we hear says the pet word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat
to wake is to become alert and attentive

explanation.surface: Something alarmed the cat and made it suddenly alert.
explanation.definitionFit: A kittiwake is a small seagull named after its call.

clue.text: Bring in some kind of reduction

indicators.note: some kind of says the word is turned into another form by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone proposes putting a cutback in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some kind of' rearranges the letters of 'reduction'.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce a measure is to bring it into use.

clue.text: Will try to have the last word on the leader

parts.note: to try is to test
amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of the second the

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to have the final say over the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a legal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: Facades of strange play

indicators.note: play here means the letters are moved freely into a new order

explanation.surface: The fronts of an odd theatrical production are described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges OFSTRANGE, the letters of 'of strange'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frontages are the faces of buildings toward a street.

clue.text: Leave for a drink

parts.note: sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to get a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To forsake is to abandon or desert.

clue.text: Had circulation, though showing no blood colour round part of it

parts.note: O looks like zero, so it stands for no or nothing

indicators.note: round tells us the colour word encloses the word for part

parts.note: blood is red
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A patient's blood flowed even though some area looked pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' is O, read as zero; 'round' sets the colour word around the small piece, splitting it R...ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to travel in a loop around something, so it circulated.

clue.text: Minister who feels jealousy about nothing

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the jealousy word goes around the letter

parts.note: envy is jealousy
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A government official resents someone over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a diplomatic minister ranking below an ambassador.

clue.text: I turn green first with giddiness

indicators.note: first says the colour word comes before the others

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone spins around and goes pale with dizziness.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic term for green; GO is a turn in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a sensation of dizziness, especially at height.

clue.text: Three feet on one limb is useful to a sailor

parts.note: a yard is three feet
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A one-legged mariner on a three-foot peg is still handy aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a yardarm is a ship's spar, so it is useful to a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either end of a ship's yard, the spar carrying a sail.

clue.text: Jewish priest cuts tail off small animal

indicators.note: cutting the tail off a word removes its last letter

parts.note: a rabbit is a small animal

explanation.surface: A religious leader trims a creature's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and leader.

clue.text: When caught without a hat, hesitates twice-he normally talks non-stop

annotationWithheld.why: When caught without a hat, hesitates twice-he normally talks non-stop: wordplay gives C + HAT + ERER, one T short; the only full parse (AT for 'When' inside HT, hat without A) has no clue word left to signal the insertion
annotationWithheld.clue: When caught without a hat, hesitates twice-he normally talks non-stop

clue.text: Quotes names

definitions.meaning: to quote a passage is to repeat it as evidence
to name someone is to mention them specifically

explanation.definitionFit: To cite is both to quote an authority and to mention someone by name, as in a citation.

clue.text: March gathering

definitions.meaning: to march is to walk in a body, as soldiers do
a gathering is a group of people or animals

explanation.definitionFit: To troop is to move together in file, and a troop is a band of people or soldiers.

clue.text: Draw the first cart back, thanks!

indicators.note: back says the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
ta is British slang for thank you

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word the, set at the end

explanation.surface: Someone pulls the leading cart backwards and says thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CART and TA together, CARTTA read backwards as ATTRAC; 'first' of 'the' gives the closing T. TA is British informal for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, pull it in.

clue.text: Irate CO was led astray by amorous material

indicators.note: being led astray means going off course, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry commanding officer was corrupted by dirty pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was led astray' rearranges IRATECO, the letters of 'Irate CO'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is literature or art dealing with sexual desire.

clue.text: Finish before the French ship For Eternity?

parts.note: finish means end
le is French for the
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A voyage ends ahead of a French vessel called Eternity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting for eternity means lasting forever, without stop.

clue.text: 24 managed to take mother to the bar

indicators.note: managed signals the letters are handled and reorganised

parts.note: the answer to clue 24, meaning a gathering of people
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A group handled taking mum down the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges TROOPMA, the 24-down answer plus MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is the bar of a pub or inn where drink is served.
